What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 1

    Discover

    1–2 weeks

    We sit with the front desk, reservations, kitchen, consultants or banquet team to map how guests actually inquire, book, arrive and complain, and which systems hold the data. We confirm what the PMS, POS, channel manager and booking systems allow through APIs or exports, and choose the first journey to automate.

    Deliverables

    • Current guest journey map with handoffs and delays
    • System and integration inventory with access options
    • Prioritized automation shortlist with indicative effort
    • Baseline measures for the chosen journey

    What we need from you

    • Read access or exports from the PMS, POS, channel manager or travel CRM
    • Time with front office, kitchen, consultant or sales leads
    • Current message templates, policies and price lists
    • WhatsApp Business account and Meta business verification status
  2. 2

    Design

    1–2 weeks

    We design conversation flows, guest forms, routing rules, response targets and approval points, and write the WhatsApp, SMS and email templates for approval. Consent wording, ID handling and retention are designed with the client's compliance owner before anything is built.

    Deliverables

    • Flow diagrams with human checkpoints marked
    • Template drafts for WhatsApp, DLT SMS and email approval
    • Data map covering consent, minimization, retention and access
    • Acceptance criteria and test scenarios

    What we need from you

    • Brand voice and approved facts for replies
    • Consent and privacy notice wording reviewed by the client's legal or compliance owner
    • Decisions on response targets, escalation owners and discount limits
  3. 3

    Build

    2–6 weeks

    We build the workflows in n8n or code, the secure guest forms and staff consoles, AI prompts grounded in approved content, and the connections to the client's systems, all in a staging setup with test data.

    Deliverables

    • Working workflows and integrations in staging
    • Secure guest forms and staff consoles
    • AI prompts with evaluation sets and refusal rules
    • Monitoring, alerts and error handling

    What we need from you

    • API credentials or integration partner access in a test environment
    • Sample anonymized data for testing
    • Feedback on staff console usability from shift leads
  4. 4

    Validate & launch

    1–2 weeks

    Staff test real scenarios: late arrivals, foreign guests, sold-out dishes, rebooked flights and changed guest counts. We check AI drafts against an evaluation set, launch on one property, outlet or desk first, and train every shift.

    Deliverables

    • Test results against acceptance criteria
    • AI draft evaluation report
    • Shift-wise training and quick reference guides
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan

    What we need from you

    • Staff time for scenario testing and training
    • Sign-off from the operations owner and the compliance owner
    • Approved templates live in the WhatsApp Business account and on DLT
  5. 5

    Operate & improve

    Ongoing, reviewed monthly

    We monitor workflow health, response targets and AI quality, fix failures, and review results with the client each month. New templates, segments, outlets and properties are added through the same approval process.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly performance and exception review
    • Workflow health and failure alerts
    • Template and prompt change log
    • Roadmap for the next journey or location

    What we need from you

    • A named operations owner for decisions
    • Feedback from shift leads and guests
    • Notice of changes to systems, policies or prices

First pilot: One property or outlet, one journey, four to six weeks

We start where volume and pain are highest. For a hotel that is usually pre-arrival messages and digital pre-check-in with Form III tracking at one property, with extras and in-stay routing added after the review. For a restaurant group it is reservations or the daily close at one outlet, and for a travel company, document and payment reminders for one desk. A first-week baseline keeps the comparison honest.

  • One property, outlet or desk and one guest journey
  • Approved WhatsApp templates and a secure guest form
  • Integration with the PMS, POS or booking system in read and limited write mode
  • A staff console for the queue, with escalation to a named manager
  • Weekly check-ins and a go or no-go review at the end of the pilot

Ways to work together

Choose the engagement that fits your stage.

  • Pilot sprint

    One automation, one segment and one accountable owner. We build, validate and measure it against agreed acceptance criteria before anything wider is committed.

    Best for: Proving value and fit with low risk

  • Phased rollout

    A prioritized roadmap across the journey, released in reviewed increments, with training and documentation after each release.

    Best for: Teams ready to connect several workflows

  • Operate & improve

    Monthly reviews of measures and exceptions, template and rule updates, and new automations as priorities change, during business hours.

    Best for: Keeping automations accurate as the business changes

Safe by design, owned by your team

  • Consent is recorded per guest and channel, service and marketing consent are kept separate, and an opt-out on any channel is applied across WhatsApp, SMS and email.
  • ID, passport and card data never enter chat or AI prompts: IDs go through secure forms with role-based access, and card payments stay with the payment gateway.
  • AI drafts, classifies and summarizes from approved content; public replies, prices, refunds, compensation and travel advice always need a named person's approval.
  • Every automated conversation offers a route to a person, and safety, medical, security, food safety and harassment messages bypass automation to the duty manager.
  • Templates, prompts and workflow changes are versioned, approved by the client owner, and registered with Meta or on DLT where required before going live.
  • Failures and missed response targets raise alerts, AI quality is sampled every month, and access is reviewed each quarter and whenever staff leave.

The obligations that shape the design

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

  • Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025

    Guest names, phone numbers, IDs, preferences and feedback are personal data. Automations are designed around clear notice, purpose-bound consent, minimal collection, security safeguards, breach response and deletion when the purpose ends. The Rules were notified on 13 November 2025 in phases: consent manager provisions from November 2026 and most business obligations from May 2027. MeitY has consulted on bringing dates forward, so we design for them now. Not legal advice.

    meity.gov.in · Source

  • Foreign guest reporting under the Immigration and Foreigners Rules 2025

    Under Rule 17, accommodation keepers must record particulars of every foreign guest, including OCI cardholders, keep them electronically for at least one year, and send Form III (formerly Form C) to the Registration Officer through the Bureau of Immigration portal within twenty-four hours of arrival, with departure details within twenty-four hours of departure. Our tools prepare and track; hotel staff verify the documents and submit.

    mha.gov.in · Source

  • WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy

    Businesses may message people only after opt-in, must use approved templates to start conversations outside the 24-hour customer service window, must honor opt-out and block requests, and must keep a prompt, clear path to a person when automation answers. The policy bars asking for full card or personal ID numbers in chat, so IDs go through a secure form. Since January 2026 Meta also bars general-purpose AI assistants; AI here serves only the business's own guest service.

    business.whatsapp.com · Source

  • TRAI commercial communication rules for SMS and calls

    Commercial SMS in India use DLT-registered headers and content templates, and promotional calls come from the designated 140 series. Under the February 2025 TCCCPR amendment, promotional content mixed into a service message makes it promotional, each promotional message must carry an opt-out, and headers carry -P, -S, -T or -G suffixes. People with registered preferences get promotions only with explicit consent. TRAI revises these rules often, so templates get rechecked.

    trai.gov.in · Source

  • Card data: RBI storage restriction and PCI DSS scope

    Since October 2022, RBI has barred entities in the card payment chain other than card issuers and networks from storing card-on-file data. Hotels and agencies that once kept card numbers to secure bookings should use gateway payment links, tokenized cards or gateway pre-authorizations, and never copy OTA virtual card details into chat or sheets. Keeping card data out of messages and our tools narrows the PCI DSS scope the business carries.

    website.rbi.org.in · Source

  • Bills and booking flows: service charge, pricing and FSSAI details

    CCPA guidelines, upheld by a single judge of the Delhi High Court in March 2025, bar hotels and restaurants from adding service charge automatically or by default, so billing and booking flows never add it on their own; check the status of any appeal. Flows show full prices upfront and avoid false urgency under the 2023 dark patterns guidelines, and FSSAI requires the 14-digit license or registration number on food bills.

    consumeraffairs.gov.in · Source

Frequently asked

Do we need to replace our PMS, POS or booking software?

No. We connect to the systems you already use through their APIs, integration partners or scheduled exports. Where a system allows only limited access, we design around it, for example by preparing data for staff to confirm rather than writing into the system directly. Naming a system on this page does not imply a partnership with its vendor.

Can we send WhatsApp messages to every guest who books?

Only to guests who have shared their number and opted in to messages from you. Outside the 24-hour window after a guest's last message, you can only send templates approved by Meta. We help you capture opt-in at booking, write templates in the right categories, and fall back to email or DLT-registered SMS for guests who have not opted in.

Will the system file Form III for foreign guests automatically?

No. Hotel staff verify the original passport and visa at arrival and submit Form III on the Bureau of Immigration portal. The automation collects the particulars in advance through a secure form, lays them out in the order the portal needs, and tracks the twenty-four-hour deadlines for arrival and departure so nothing slips on a busy night.

Will AI reply to guests and reviews on its own?

In chat, AI answers routine questions only from approved information such as check-in times, menus or itinerary details, and hands over to a person when it is unsure or the guest asks. Public review replies, prices, refunds, compensation, visa guidance and anything involving safety are always approved or handled by a named member of your team.

How do you handle guest IDs, passports and card details?

IDs and passports are collected only through a secure form on your domain, stored encrypted, visible to front office or consultant roles, and deleted on a schedule you approve, with Form III records kept for the period the Rules require. We never ask for ID numbers or card numbers in chat, and card payments go through your payment gateway's hosted links.

Can this work with Swiggy and Zomato?

Yes, through your POS or an aggregator integration partner that supports menu and item availability actions, and through the reports and exports the partner dashboards provide. We do not scrape partner apps or copy customer data out of them against their terms. Where an action is not available through an integration, the automation alerts the outlet manager to make the change.

How long until something is live, and what does it cost?

Most first pilots run four to six weeks from kickoff to a live journey at one property, outlet or desk. Cost depends on the systems involved, the number of locations and the journeys in scope, so we quote after the Discover phase rather than publishing a fixed price.

We also host international guests. Does this work with GDPR?

The same principles apply: purpose-based consent, minimal data, clear retention and access controls. If you market to or monitor people in the EU or UK, GDPR may apply alongside India's DPDP Act, so we configure notices, consent records and deletion rules in a way your legal adviser can confirm against both.
